title: Continuous Improvement of Abrasive Waterjet Cutting Process of Kevlar Fiber-Reinforced Composites: A Systematic DISMO-Based Approach
content: Aligned with Six Sigma principles and continuous improvement, this study applies the structured DISMO methodology, supported by VBA software tools, to identify suitable operating conditions for abrasive waterjet machining (AWJC) of Kevlar ﬁber composites. Starting from ten machining output parameters evaluating process performance and productivity, rank correlation analysis prioritized the kerf taper angle (ka) and material removal rate (MRR). A screening phase using the random balance method reduced the input factors from six to three key factors: traverse speed (v), focusing tube diameter (D), and abrasive ﬂow rate (q). First-order polynomial empirical models were established to quantify parameter eﬀects. Multi-response optimization using a composite desirability function identiﬁed a balanced operating regime (v = 500mm/min, D = 0.76 mm și q = 200 g/min) with a desirability value of Ds = 0.70. This moderate value highlights the inherent trade-oﬀ between maximizing material removal rate and minimizing taper angle. Due to its general character, the developed methodological framework can be easily adapted for the analysis and control of other manufacturing processes.
